elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Renewal remains automatic ("Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term"), and the conditional preferred elements are not all satisfied: the opt-out window is 60 (not ≤30) days, no Vendor reminder is added, the renewal term is not fixed at ≤12 months, and the uplift cap is 105% rather than the lesser of CPI and 3%.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Retained language ties each renewal to "an additional term equal in duration to the previous term," so a Service Option Attachment with an initial term longer than 12 months renews for that longer period; no 12-month ceiling was inserted.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Redline sets notice at "at least 60 days prior to the end of the then-current term," which exceeds the 30-day preferred opt-out.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered language; Section 3.2 as amended imposes only a mutual notice right, not an IBM pre-renewal reminder.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Inserted cap is "will not exceed 105% of the charges in effect for the immediately preceding term" — a flat 5% ceiling with no CPI comparator or 3% limit.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Amended Section 3.2 reads "unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least 60 days prior to the end of the then-current term." The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a pattern artefact (the clause uses plain figures "60" rather than the document's "sixty (60)" convention); on substance the window is exactly 60 days and within the fallback ceiling.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: New sentence: "Charges for each renewal term will not exceed 105% of the charges in effect for the immediately preceding term of the applicable Service Option Attachment" — an express 5% ceiling on renewal-term charges.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the non-renewal window is reduced from 90 to 60 days and renewal charges are capped at 105% of the prior term. The finding's 'deviation' classification and fallback targeting are correct, since the original 90-day window and uncapped renewal pricing both failed the fallback.

Preferred level fails on four counts, correctly noted rather than redlined: renewal term is still 'equal in duration to the previous term' (no 12-month cap), opt-out is 60 not 30 days, there is no IBM 60-day reminder, and the uplift cap is 5% rather than the lesser of CPI and 3%.

Minimality holds: only the notice figure was changed and one short cap sentence added; Section 13.1's mid-term change right, non-retroactivity and Customer's 30-day no-charge termination election are retained verbatim, and no unrelated words were deleted.
Drafting nit for the drafter (not a defect): conform the inserted figure to the document's convention — 'sixty (60) days' — so the number matches surrounding usage and passes automated term checks.

Residual risk to flag to the client, not a checklist failure: Section 13.1 still lets IBM change Service Option Attachment prices on 90 days' notice with no percentage limit; because the new cap is measured against 'charges in effect for the immediately preceding term,' a mid-term 13.1 increase resets the baseline. If we want the 5% ceiling to be airtight, add 'notwithstanding Section 13.1' or measure the cap against charges in effect on the applicable Service Option Attachment Start Date — but Customer's 30-day no-charge termination election under 13.1 mitigates this, so the current edit remains defensible as-is.

Also consider asymmetric drafting: the mutual 60-day figure shortens IBM's own non-renewal notice from 90 to 60 days, reducing Customer's warning of an IBM exit. Preserving 90 days for IBM while cutting Customer's window to 60 would be strictly more protective, though the single-number edit is the simpler minimal change.
